Export a complete plain-text OpenSesame experiment

Source: R/scripting.R
export_opensesame.Rd

Writes <base>.osexp and the two tables it reads. Its loop runs over <base>_opensesame.csv, which holds numbers only: lexsync_row (the trial's position in loop order, from 1), lexsync_trial, lexsync_list, lexsync_set, the trigger codes, critical_region and any per-trial duration. The presented text, condition, block and answer are in <base>_opensesame_text.csv, which the inline scripts read with Python's csv module, so OpenSesame never evaluates them. Copy both tables with the experiment.

Usage

export_opensesame(stimuli, design, schema, outdir, base = NULL)

Arguments

stimuli

Stimuli with trigger columns (see assign_triggers()).

design

A parsed design configuration.

schema

The parsed global schema (trigger and presentation settings).

outdir

Output directory.

base

Optional file-name stem. By default the design's design_stem().

Value

The path to the generated .osexp, version 1's when there are several, invisibly.

Details

Before the loop, an inline script, lexsync_instructions, shows the design's instructions, or lexsync's for its task, and waits for the space bar. Every trial is logged. A response after a text event is collected by that event's script from the stimulus's onset, which sets response, response_time, timed_out and correct. A response kept after the stimulus with from: offset is a keyboard_response, and a script after it sets timed_out and correct. Self-paced reading sets lexsync_region_rts and a question question_response and question_rt. A script clears these as each trial starts, another copies the trial's labels into lexsync_condition, lexsync_block and lexsync_answer, and a logger item ends the trial.

Every canvas a trial shows is built before the trial runs, in the prepare phase of its script, and each event is timed from the onset its display returns. An event ends half a frame before its duration is up, so that the next display lands on the refresh that ends it. The frame period is measured at start-up and logged as lexsync_frame_ms, with presentation.assumed_refresh_hz as the fallback when the measurement fails. Each trigger code is held for triggers.trigger_hold_ms, at least 10 ms, through the events after it when its own is shorter, unless the next onset's code replaces it first. The session markers, 254 and 255, are sent just before the first trial and just after the last, held the same way.

The setup writes the codes to the parallel port at triggers.parallel_address or, with triggers.backend: serial, as single bytes to triggers.serial_port at triggers.baudrate. When that device cannot be opened, triggers.mode: auto prints the codes instead. An inline script, lexsync_trigger_notice, then says so before any other screen and waits for the C key. hardware stops the experiment there, and mock prints the codes without trying the device. Every trial logs lexsync_trigger_mode, hardware or mock. Text is drawn presentation.text_height_px pixels high, OpenSesame's font_size, and OpenSesame takes full screen from the mode it is launched in.

A design with more than one presentation version, one per (replicate, list) pair of the trials, gets one experiment per version instead, each with its own two tables holding only that version's trials: <base>_list<k>.osexp, or <base>_rep<r>_list<k>.osexp when the versions span several replicates. Each one checks OpenSesame's subject number at start-up and shows a warning when that participant would normally run another version. A design with counterbalance.orders: m gets one experiment per version and order, <base>_list<k>_order<j>.osexp (<base>_order<j>.osexp for a single version), each with tables sorted by its order, a lexsync_order variable that every trial logs, and a check that compares the participant's order too, order (((p - 1) div V) mod m) + 1. export_experiments() lists every file written.

OpenSesame evaluates the cells of a loop table: in 4.x a cell holding { runs as a Python f-string, and in 3.3 a cell starting with = or holding [=...] runs as Python. A value in a numeric column that is not a plain number is therefore refused, naming the column. An empty cell passes. These rules were checked against the sources of OpenSesame 3.3.14 and 4.1.20.
